# 100-identity API v3 broker qualification

On November 18, 2026, the live sandbox accepted 100 distinct TLS-authenticated
clients across host-a, host-e, and host-f. The synthetic text workload created 108
PRs. Native Actions and Git receipts verify 100 merges and eight excluded,
retired heads. Six retirements were cross-host reassignments. Two were conflicting
additions replaced by explicit resolutions preserving both contributions.

| Initial 100 operations | Status polls | Retryable HTTP responses | Transport retries |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Publication | 2,923 | 0 | 2 |
| Registration | 220 | 0 | 10 |

The earlier 60-identity run observed 11,937 publication polls and 531 retryable
registration responses. Workload size and live GitHub timing varied between runs.
The measured intervals from the six scheduler reassignment receipts to observed
broker retirement were 44.3–56.4 seconds. These were
measured using scheduler receipt timestamps and the broker journal under the
original single-build setting. The earlier run observed roughly seven to ten
minutes. The successor grant continued to require observed retirement.

PRs #279 and #314 were held after
conflicting with landed edits. The resolutions went through native Actions and
preserved both contributions in each shared file. Git verified all
98 expected final paths. The final sandbox
main was `7a4110c4fdd69ba891474572d8132389eee955fa`. Each broker integration receipt was compared with
the exact first-parent Git merge, GitHub merge event, and successful Actions
merge-group run. Forge summary SHA disagreements were recorded separately
(#255, #264). No manual statuses were used.

The harness resumed from existing receipts after GitHub returned HTTP 422
during concurrent PR identity reads. It verified the PR identities in small
GraphQL batches before freezing all 100 exact heads. Permission probes on all
three hosts confirmed the worker role remained bounded.

The main ruleset's build capacity was temporarily raised from one to 30
after the six queued handoffs retired and was restored before final
verification. Native Actions App 15368, the PR requirement, ALLGREEN, one
entry per merge, and no bypass actors remained in force. All temporary
identities and private keys were removed. The broker stayed at API v3.

The deployed source was `924dc161e80b440fd70d1673c0e1419a0333c9a2`. All 82 coordinator and
broker regressions passed on macOS, host-a, host-e, and host-f. This run used the
MIT-derived recovery branch and independently authored tooling. Post-MIT
upstream remained black-box. It qualifies the exercised sandbox workload
with synthetic clients and small text edits. Follow-up product scope includes
binary, deletion, and file-mode publication, dependency scheduling, and
provider-failure tests at live scale.
